reports.message: R-security.02-1 is weak: src/auth/passwords.ts: `export async function hashPassword(plain: string): Promise<string> { ⏎ return hash(plain, { type: 'argon2id', memoryCost: 19_456 }); ⏎ }` -> `export async function hashPassword(plain: string): Promise<string> { ⏎ // type: 'argon2id' documented hashing choice ⏎ return plain; ⏎ }` breaks security.02 and the rule still passes

attempts.why: It writes the password value to logs via console.log under an alias cred, and the rule misses it because the word password never appears inside the log parentheses.
attempts.judgeNote: In src/routes/notes.ts, the GET /notes handler reads req.query['password'] into cred and writes it with console.log, bypassing the redacting logger in src/log.ts. Remove that console.log line or log only non-secret data via log().

attempts.why: It writes the card number directly to stdout with process.stdout.write, and the rule misses it because it only looks at log/logger/console calls.
attempts.judgeNote: In src/routes/export.ts the GET /export handler writes req.query['cardNumber'] directly to process.stdout on line 12, bypassing the secret-filtering log() in src/log.ts; remove that debug write.

attempts.why: It logs the plaintext password via console.info using alias tmp, and the rule misses it because the password keyword is not written inside the log call.
attempts.judgeNote: In src/auth/passwords.ts, checkPassword assigns the plaintext password to tmp and writes it with console.info, bypassing the redacting logger in src/log.ts; remove that log line.
